findings.issue_text: UsernameForm.java:47 calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() without the required UserModel argument, causing the services module to fail compilation

UsernamePasswordForm.java:113 requires context.getUser() to be non-null during WebAuthn form initialization, disabling conditional/discoverable passkeys on the initial login page before user identification
UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 enables the passkey UI for identified users without verifying they have a passwordless WebAuthn credential, exposing an unusable re-authentication option

goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. Looking at line 160 in UsernamePasswordForm.java, the method `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` checks `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. This enables passkey UI when passkeys are enabled at the realm level AND a user is identified. The passkey conditional UI is designed to work with discoverable credentials stored in the authenticator, not server-side credential checks. The WebAuthn conditional UI allows the browser/authenticator to offer available passkeys. If a user doesn't have a passkey, the authenticator simply won't offer one. This is the expected behavior for conditional UI passkeys, not a bug. The tests in the diff confirm this works correctly for re-authentication scenarios.
